For the data set $4, 7, 9, 11, 14, 15, 21$, find the median and the range.
questions.guidance: The median is the middle value, $11$. The range is $21-4=17$.

questions.question: A data set has $Q_1=42$, $Q_3=68$, minimum $15$ and maximum $112$. Find the upper fence.
questions.guidance: IQR $=68-42=26$. Upper fence $=Q_3+1.5\times IQR=68+39=107$.

The heights of a group of students are approximately normally distributed with mean $168$ cm and standard deviation $6$ cm. Using the 68-95-99.7 rule, find the percentage of students with heights between $156$ cm and $180$ cm.
questions.guidance: $156$ and $180$ are two standard deviations below and above the mean, so approximately $95\%$ lie in this interval.

questions.question: For a least squares line $y=84-2.5x$, which statement is correct?
options: For each increase of 1 in $x$, the predicted value of $y$ increases by $2.5$.
For each increase of 1 in $x$, the predicted value of $y$ decreases by $2.5$.
When $x=0$, the predicted value of $y$ is $-2.5$.
questions.guidance: The slope is $-2.5$, so each increase of 1 in $x$ decreases predicted $y$ by $2.5$.

questions.question: The least squares line for predicting price, in dollars, from age, in years, is $\text{price}=420000-8500\times\text{age}$. Find the predicted price of a $12$-year-old property.
For a data set, Pearson's correlation coefficient is $r=-0.72$. Find the coefficient of determination as a percentage, correct to one decimal place.
questions.guidance: $r^2=(-0.72)^2=0.5184$, so the coefficient of determination is $51.8\%$.

questions.question: A residual is calculated as
questions.guidance: Residual $=$ actual response value $-$ predicted response value.

questions.question: A model predicts $\hat y=1250$ for a value whose actual observed value is $1175$. Find the residual.
A seasonal index for quarter 3 is $1.25$. If the actual value in quarter 3 is $340$, find the deseasonalised value.
questions.guidance: Deseasonalised value $=\frac{340}{1.25}=272$.

questions.question: If a seasonal index is $0.80$, then compared with the average season, that season is
questions.guidance: A seasonal index of $0.80$ means the season is $80\%$ of average, or $20\%$ lower than average.

questions.question: The values for days 1 to 5 of a time series are $18, 22, 25, 19, 30$. Find the three-median smoothed value for day 3.
questions.guidance: For day 3, use days 2, 3 and 4: $22,25,19$. Their median is $22$.

questions.question: A sequence is defined by $u_0=500$ and $u_{n+1}=1.04u_n+30$. Find $u_2$, correct to the nearest cent.
An investment of $P$ dollars earns interest at $6\%$ per annum compounding monthly. The monthly recurrence multiplier is
questions.guidance: The monthly interest rate is $0.06/12=0.005$, so the multiplier is $1.005$.

questions.question: A loan balance follows $L_0=120000$, $L_{n+1}=1.006L_n-850$. Find the interest charged in the first month.
questions.guidance: Interest in the first month is $0.006\times120000=720$.

questions.question: A car worth $36000$ depreciates by the flat-rate method to $21600$ after $4$ years. Find the annual flat-rate depreciation amount.
questions.guidance: Total depreciation is $36000-21600=14400$. Over 4 years, annual depreciation is $14400/4=3600$.

questions.question: A machine worth $50000$ depreciates by $12\%$ per year using reducing balance depreciation. Its value after $n$ years is
questions.guidance: Reducing balance depreciation by $12\%$ means the value is multiplied by $0.88$ each year.

questions.question: Equipment is bought for $18000$ and depreciates by $15\%$ per year using reducing balance depreciation. Find its value after $3$ years, correct to the nearest dollar.
questions.guidance: $V_3=18000(0.85)^3=11054.25$, so the value is approximately $11054$.

questions.question: An item worth $24000$ depreciates by unit cost depreciation at $1.80$ per kilometre. If it is used for $4500$ km, find its new value.
A perpetuity has principal $300000$ and earns $4.8\%$ per annum. The annual payment that can be made forever is
questions.guidance: Annual perpetuity payment $=300000\times0.048=14400$.

questions.question: An account starts with $2500$ and earns $3.9\%$ per annum compounding monthly. No deposits or withdrawals are made. Find the balance after $2$ years, correct to the nearest cent.
A savings account has $A_0=6000$ and $A_{n+1}=1.002A_n+120$, where $n$ is measured in months. Find $A_1$.
A $400000$ loan is charged interest at $5.4\%$ per annum compounding monthly. Monthly repayments are $2500$. Write a recurrence relation for the loan balance $L_n$ after $n$ months.
questions.guidance: Monthly interest rate is $0.054/12=0.0045$. Therefore $L_0=400000$ and $L_{n+1}=1.0045L_n-2500$.

questions.question: If matrix $A$ has order $3\times 2$ and matrix $B$ has order $2\times 4$, then $AB$ has order
questions.guidance: A $3\times2$ matrix multiplied by a $2\times4$ matrix gives a $3\times4$ matrix.

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}5\\7\end{bmatrix}$. Find $AB$.
questions.guidance: $AB=\begin{bmatrix}2(5)+(-1)(7)\\3(5)+4(7)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\43\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.question: The matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$ is
questions.guidance: A square matrix with 1s on the leading diagonal and 0s elsewhere is an identity matrix.

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}4&7\\2&5\end{bmatrix}$. Find $\det(A)$.
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$. Find the element in row 2, column 1 of $A^2$.
questions.guidance: $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}7&10\\15&22\end{bmatrix}$, so the row 2, column 1 element is $15$.

questions.question: A transition matrix has columns that each sum to
questions.guidance: In this course convention, transition matrices use columns for current state, so each column sums to 1.

questions.question: A transition matrix is $M=\begin{bmatrix}0.8&0.3\\0.2&0.7\end{bmatrix}$ and $S_0=\begin{bmatrix}100\\50\end{bmatrix}$. Find $S_1=MS_0$.
questions.guidance: $S_1=\begin{bmatrix}0.8(100)+0.3(50)\\0.2(100)+0.7(50)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}95\\55\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.question: A population vector is $P_0=\begin{bmatrix}40\\60\end{bmatrix}$ and $P_{n+1}=\begin{bmatrix}0.6&0.2\\0.4&0.8\end{bmatrix}P_n$. Find the total population after one transition.
questions.guidance: $P_1=\begin{bmatrix}0.6(40)+0.2(60)\\0.4(40)+0.8(60)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}36\\64\end{bmatrix}$. Total $=100$.

questions.question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$, the inverse exists because
questions.guidance: $\det(A)=2(3)-1(5)=1\ne0$, so the inverse exists.

questions.question: A permutation sends the order $(A,B,C,D)$ to $(C,A,D,B)$. Starting from $(A,B,C,D)$, what is the order after applying the same permutation twice?
questions.guidance: First application gives $(C,A,D,B)$. Apply the same positions again: new order becomes $(D,C,B,A)$.

questions.question: A graph has $8$ vertices and $11$ edges. If it is connected and planar, find the number of faces.
questions.guidance: Euler's formula gives $v+f=e+2$. Hence $8+f=11+2$, so $f=5$.

questions.question: A connected graph has exactly two vertices of odd degree. Which statement is true?
options: It has an Eulerian circuit but no Eulerian trail.
It has an Eulerian trail but no Eulerian circuit.
It has neither an Eulerian trail nor an Eulerian circuit.
questions.guidance: A connected graph has an Eulerian trail if exactly two vertices have odd degree, and an Eulerian circuit if all vertices have even degree.

questions.question: A tree has $13$ vertices. How many edges does it have?
questions.guidance: A tree with $v$ vertices has $v-1$ edges. Hence $13-1=12$.

questions.question: In a simple connected graph with vertices $A,B,C,D$, a route that visits each vertex exactly once is called
questions.guidance: A Hamiltonian path visits each vertex exactly once.

questions.question: A network has edges with weights $AB=4$, $AC=6$, $BC=3$, $BD=5$, $CD=2$. Find the weight of the minimum spanning tree.
questions.guidance: Choose the smallest edges that connect all vertices without a cycle: $CD=2$, $BC=3$, $AB=4$. Total $=9$.

questions.question: A shortest path from $S$ to $T$ has edge weights $7, 4, 9$ along the selected route. Find the length of this path.
questions.guidance: Total path length $=7+4+9=20$.

questions.question: For a maximum flow problem, the maximum flow is equal to
options: the number of edges in the network
the capacity of the minimum cut
the capacity of the maximum cut
the sum of all edge capacities
questions.guidance: By the max-flow min-cut theorem, maximum flow equals the capacity of the minimum cut.

questions.question: A cut in a flow network crosses edges with capacities $12$, $9$, $4$ and $15$. Find the capacity of the cut.
questions.guidance: Cut capacity $=12+9+4+15=40$.

questions.question: A project has activities $A,B,C,D$ with durations $A=3$, $B=5$, $C=4$, $D=6$. Activity $D$ cannot start until both $B$ and $C$ are complete; $B$ and $C$ cannot start until $A$ is complete. Find the minimum completion time.
questions.guidance: After $A$, $B$ and $C$ run in parallel. The longer is $B=5$. Then $D=6$. Minimum time $=3+5+6=14$.

questions.question: In the Hungarian algorithm for a minimisation problem, the first step is usually to
options: add the largest value in each row to all entries in that row
subtract the smallest value in each row from all entries in that row
multiply each row by its smallest value
delete all rows that contain a zero
questions.guidance: For a minimisation assignment problem, the row reduction step subtracts the smallest value in each row.

questions.question: Three workers $A,B,C$ are to be assigned to three jobs $1,2,3$. The costs are $A:(9,4,7)$, $B:(6,8,5)$, $C:(5,7,6)$. Find the minimum total cost.
questions.guidance: Check assignments: $A2+B3+C1=4+5+5=14$, which is minimal.

questions.question: A data set has mean $24$ and standard deviation $5$. A value has standardised score $z=-1.4$. Find the original value.
The recurrence $V_0=18000$, $V_{n+1}=V_n-1500$ models
questions.guidance: The value decreases by the same dollar amount each period, so it is flat rate depreciation.

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&5\\0&2\end{bmatrix}$. Find the element in row 1, column 2 of $AB$.
questions.guidance: Row 1 of $A$ times column 2 of $B$: $3(5)+1(2)=17$.

questions.question: A connected graph has vertex degrees $3,3,2,2,2,2$. Does it have an Eulerian circuit? Answer yes or no.
questions.guidance: An Eulerian circuit requires all vertices to have even degree. There are two vertices of odd degree, so it does not have an Eulerian circuit.

questions.question: A least squares model is fitted to data with $r=0.91$. Which description best matches the linear association?
questions.guidance: Since $r=0.91$ is close to $1$, the association is strong and positive.
